{{Short description|French biologist (born 1973)}}
{{Expand French|topic=bio|date=November 2019}}

'''Olivier Voinnet''' (born 1972)<ref name="6profs">{{cite web|url=https://www.nzz.ch/sechs-neue-eth-professoren-1.5253890|title=Sechs neue ETH-Professoren|work=[[Neue Zürcher Zeitung]]}}</ref> is a French biologist and professor of RNA biology at the [[ETH Zurich]].<ref name="roessler">{{cite web|url=https://www.ethlife.ethz.ch/archive_articles/130613_roesslerpreis_voinnet_per/index_EN.html|title=Extraordinary researcher honoured|author=|work=ethlife.ethz.ch}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://sites.google.com/site/voinnetlab/|title=Voinnet Lab|work=google.com}}</ref> Voinnet obtained his PhD in 2001 in England in the group of [[David Baulcombe]] and later obtained a position as an independent group leader at the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique|CNRS]] in Strasbourg where he was promoted to ''Directeur de Recherche'' in 2005. In 2010, he moved to  [[ETH Zurich]] where he was appointed a full professor of RNA Biology.<ref name="6profs"/><ref name="roessler"/> Voinnet's published articles have been subject to allegations of image manipulation, leading to multiple corrections and retractions: as of 2022 nine of Voinnet's scientific articles have been retracted, five others have received an expression of concern, and 25 others have been corrected.<ref>{{cite web |title=Retraction Watch Database - Voinnet |url=http://retractiondatabase.org/RetractionSearch.aspx#?auth%3dVoinnet%252c%2bOlivier |website=Retraction Watch |publisher=Center for Scientific Integrity |accessdate=2022-06-30}}</ref>

==Investigations of scientific misconduct==

In 2015, Voinnet's work was investigated for image manipulation.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2015/04/allegations-under-investigation.html|title=Allegations under investigation|work=ethz.ch}}</ref> The investigation at ETH Zurich found that the scientist "breached his duty of care in the handling of figures as well as in his supervisory duties as a research director...and will receive an admonition in relation to his conduct," but also concluded that "this is not a case of scientific misconduct as defined in ETH Zurich's Rules of Procedure".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2015/07/investigation-result-voinnet.html|author=Press release|title=Conducted properly – published incorrectly|work=ethz.ch}}</ref> Another, independent investigation by CNRS established "the existence of deliberate chart/diagram manipulations, in breach of the ethical standards applicable to the presentation of scientific results," but such "inappropriate presentation of experimental data...does not amount to fabrication."<ref name="cnrs_investigation">{{cite web|url=http://www2.cnrs.fr/en/2593.htm|title=Completion of the procedure against Olivier Voinnet|author=Press release|work=cnrs.fr}}</ref>

==Bans, suspensions==

In July 2015, Voinnet was suspended from the [[CNRS]] (the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]]) for 2 years.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sciences.blogs.liberation.fr/home/2015/07/le-cnrs-exclut-olivier-voinnet.html|title=Le CNRS exclut Olivier Voinnet|work=liberation.fr|access-date=2015-07-10|archive-date=2015-07-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150713021323/http://sciences.blogs.liberation.fr/home/2015/07/le-cnrs-exclut-olivier-voinnet.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://retractionwatch.com/2015/07/10/high-profile-biologist-is-suspended-after-two-investigations-found-he-breached-his-duty-of-care-committed-misconduct/|title=High-profile biologist is suspended after two investigations found he "breached his duty of care", committed "misconduct"|work=retractionwatch.com|date=2015-07-10}}</ref> In January 2016 the [[SNSF]] (the [[Swiss National Science Foundation]]) terminated Voinnet's funding, and banned him from additional funding for three years.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://retractionwatch.com/2016/01/26/swiss-funding-agency-cuts-off-voinnet-bans-him-for-3-years/|title=Swiss funding agency cuts off Voinnet, bans him for 3 years|work=retractionwatch.com|date=2016-01-26}}</ref>

==Awards==

In 2009 Voinnet was awarded the [[EMBO Gold Medal]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://embo.org/news/press-releases/press-releases-2009/olivier-voinnet-awarded-2009-embo-gold-medal|title=Olivier Voinnet awarded 2009 EMBO Gold Medal|author=|work=embo.org|access-date=2016-01-29|archive-date=2016-03-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160314095945/http://embo.org/news/press-releases/press-releases-2009/olivier-voinnet-awarded-2009-embo-gold-medal|url-status=dead}}</ref> The [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] (EMBO) retracted the award in 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://retractionwatch.com/2016/01/28/embo-takes-back-voinnets-award-investigates-other-awardee-who-just-lost-a-nature-genetics-paper/|title=EMBO takes back Voinnet's award, investigates other awardee who just lost a Nature Genetics paper|work=retractionwatch.com|date=2016-01-28}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the-scientist.com/?articles.view/articleNo/45183/title/Funding-Ban-for-Plant-Biologist/|title=Funding Ban for Plant Biologist|work=the-scientist.com}}</ref> In 2009 he was also awarded the "[[Grand Prix scientifique de la Fondation Louis D.]]" of the [[Institut de France]].<ref>[http://grands-prix.institut-de-france.fr/olivier-voinnet-et-herve-vaucheret Olivier Voinnet et Hervé Vaucheret] - website of the [[Institut de France]]</ref>

In 2013 he was awarded the [[Rössler Prize]] at the [[ETH]] Zurich, sponsored by [[Max Rössler]]. This prize is awarded each year to a young professor from ETH Zurich, considered to be of the ″most promising young scientists in the further development of their career″.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ethz.ch/en/research/science-awards-and-events/roessler-prize.html|title=Rössler Prize|author=|work=eth.ch}}</ref>
